business_question: Does Alphabet's revenue concentration in the European Union create hidden exposure to EU digital regulation enforcement?
description: Alphabet derives approximately 30% of Google revenue from the EMEA region, with the European Union representing the largest regulatory jurisdiction outside the United States. The EU Digital Markets Act (DMA) designated Alphabet as a Gatekeeper in September 2023, with enforcement obligations from March 2024. The DMA requires Alphabet to open its platforms (Google Search, Google Play, Chrome, Google Maps) to third-party competitors, prohibits self-preferencing, and imposes interoperability requirements. Non-compliance carries fines of up to 10% of global revenue. An investor holding Alphabet may not recognise that its European revenue concentration creates a structural regulatory exposure that could require fundamental changes to its highest-margin business lines.
